entries.e: Pangaea, a supercontinent consisting of virtually all of the earth's landmass, that broke up towards the end of the Triassic.
Laurasia, one of the two supercontinents that formed after the breakup of Pangaea; consisted of most of the landmass that forms part of the Northern Hemisphere.
Panthalassa, the ocean that surrounded Pangaea.
Gondwana, one of the two supercontinents that formed from the southern half of Pangaea after its breakup; its remnants make up most of the earth's present continental land area.
Banihal, the name of a village and a pass located to the south of the Kashmir Valley in the Pir Panjal range.
Pir Panjal, the name of the mountain range to the south and west of the Kashmir Valley.
the name of a district in the northern part of the Kashmir Valley, officially known as Baramulla
the name of a locality near the town of Baramulla, where Xuanzang spent his first night in Kashmir.
Mt. Harmukh, located in the district of Ganderbal, towards the north-east of the Kashmir Valley; its peak elevation is about 5300m ASL, and it is revered by Kashmiri Pandits as the abode of Shiva.

Pandrethan, the name of a locality to the south-east of Srinagar, possibly the site of the Śrīnagarī supposedly founded by Ashoka, with the name later transferred to the contiguous Pravarapura, the modern-day Srinagar.
the name of a village in the Pulwama district, towards the centre-southern region of the Kashmir Valley, officially known as Khrew.

Burzahom, the name of a site towards the north-east of Srinagar city, where remnants of a Neolithic and Megalithic culture contemporaneous with and outlasting the Mature Phase of the Indus Valley Civilization, including skeletal remains, ha
Parihaspore, the name of a town that the 8th century king of Kashmir, Lalitaditya Muktapida, built as his capital, 22 km northwest of Srinagar, atop a plateau (see وُڈٕر (vuḍụr)).
a small circular, or wheel-shaped, piece of leather, wood, or metal, used for fastening the chain of a bolt, etc.
a large sheet of some material
someone who is walking on the way
to move away from the path
one who causes the path to be lost
to be lost from the path
to be set to the way
dative ablative locative singular of وَتھ (vath)
demonic possession supposedly caused by walking alone on a dark road, causing convulsions in a baby, frenzy and delirium, and possibly miscarriage in women (possession sense of پٲنٛتھُن)
Plural and compound form of وَتھ (vath) (“way, path, road”).
one who, while en route with a caravan or a number of companions, abandons them and absconds
one who travels on a road
a roadside village; especially when seldom occurring on a lonely road
to put an amulet containing a charm on someone, for protection against evil spirits
coming and going backwards and forwards, the cycle of rebirth; trouble, worry, running hither and thither
to rise, to become high (of something sunk)
the profession of a tradesman; trade
a Kashmiri Brahmin, especially an educated one
3rd person interrogative form of the present-tense copula ("to be"), corresponding to declarative چھُ (chu) and چھےٚ (che).
Pashto, an Iranic language natively spoken by Pashtuns
to commit suicide, to kill oneself
Pampore, the name of a town and tehsil in the Pulwama district of the southern part of the Kashmir Valley; the broader region around it has been famous for saffron cultivation from antiquity
a means, expedient, or contrivance (to do something successfully)
capitalism, a socio-economic system based on the private ownership of the means of production and the exploitation of profits
Karbala (a city in central Iraq, site of the murder of Husayn ibn Ali and major pilgrimage destination for Shiite Muslims)
Chenab (a river in Punjab, Pakistan and the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the state of Himachal Pradesh in India)
one who is skilled in recognizing
chopped up barley straw and chaff
gaining or inducing agreement, consent, or compliance
hardship on the neck; that hardship which does not go away easily
a cloth used as a spread
to be set on the wrong path
to be set on the correct path
to set on the correct path
to cause one to be ashamed everywhere
